title: Planar Graph Embedding Formalization for Euler Formula

problemStatement.formal: For planar graph builds, V-E+F=2 is preserved by spanning-tree and cycle-edge construction; 5-degeneracy gives a six-color bound, and Euler edge bounds rule out K_5 and K_{3,3}.
problemStatement.plain: Extends Euler's polyhedral formula V-E+F=2 to planar graph theory: spanning tree approach, graph degeneracy (5-degenerate), and the Six Color Theorem via degeneracy coloring.
whyMatters: Euler's V-E+F relation becomes a working engine for planar graph coloring and nonplanarity results.
Degeneracy converts geometric embedding constraints into algorithmic color bounds.
The proof cluster is a useful bridge from polyhedra to planar graph theory and the six-color theorem.

proven: `KDegenerate`, `planar_five_degenerate`, `six_colorable_from_degeneracy`, `degeneracy_color_count`, and `planar_color_bound` connect planar edge bounds with coloring.
`edge_bound_simple`, `edge_bound_bipartite`, `k5_not_planar`, `k33_not_planar`, and `petersen_not_planar` package standard planar obstruction results.
open: `EulerPolyhedralOQ01.lean` documents zero axioms and zero sorries; the parent `EulerPolyhedralFormula.lean` still has the general `euler_formula_axiom`.
knownResults.goal: Present the planar graph consequences as a clean axiom-free extension while distinguishing them from the older parent axiom.
